title: Storage engines and relation boundaries
summary: FILE, OBJECT, explicitly projected JSON, native SQLite read-only/GeoPackage and federated providers retain independent storage contracts. SQLiteWritableDatabaseEngine (development candidate v0.89-v0.91) is a separate, opt-in read/write backend. It reuses NoSQLServer SQL semantics, snapshots committed SQLite/WAL state with sqlite3_backup, and executes NoSQL-approved typed prepared mutations via a small native bridge.
invariants: JSON crosses into relations only through explicit row/column projections.
The original native SQLite/GeoPackage page reader remains read-only. Opt-in writable SQLite uses a separate engine and native SQLite write bridge; do not infer write support for GeoPackage.
GeoPackage adds typed geometry over native SQLite transport.
Provider semantics remain outside NoSQLServer; SQL scanning a relation does not make the relation's producer policy truth.
No raw user SQL is handed to SQLite as the NoSQLServer query evaluator; the native bridge is responsible for prepared mutation execution and consistent backup snapshots.
Storage Fabric and MI/MU distributed authority are not conferred by a local SQLite database file.
